agent_vs_you: The agent trusted the catalogue line 'lettering: true GUARANTEES designed lettering spelled exactly' and put the whole 108-character address in as ONE quoted string, in a single qwen render at 1:1 then a centre crop. It gave no size hierarchy or line plan for the address, and it dropped the user's 'black-and-cream' from the prompt (the planner prompt even uses 'black and cream' as its example of user words to keep). I treat a 108-character address as small print that a 640 px diffusion model will not spell reliably. I would let qwen letter only the three short lines, which it got right in both renders, and set the address with the one tool that guarantees exact characters: text-overlay, by code. The agent could not choose that split. The planner rule says 'One node per designed piece; never a picture node plus a text-overlay for the same design', the WORDS rule sends every flyer word to lettering:true, and nothing in the catalogue says lettering degrades with string length. What sank the output was the harness. Its single fix told qwen to letter the address while also deleting the 'Third address line' and 'Fourth address line' entirely. The fix broke the two lines that had been correct, nothing re-read the result, and the node was marked done with the note 'lettering fixed'.

your_plan.say: I'll letter the headline, date and time into a clean black-and-cream 4:5 flyer with the lower half left empty, then set the full address by code so every letter, dash, comma and apostrophe is exact.

params.prompt_or_change: Clean minimalist typographic flyer, portrait. Solid flat black background. All lettering in warm cream (#F3E9D2), one bold geometric sans-serif, centred, generous margins. In the TOP HALF only: very large "Printmakers' Open Studio" on two lines (a straight typewriter apostrophe); under it, medium size, "9 October 2027"; on the next line "11:00–17:00". The whole lower half is empty flat black: no text, no lines, no shapes, no texture. No other words, no logo, no border, no illustration.

steps.why: qwen lettered these three short strings correctly in both of the agent's renders. With aspect 4:5 and lettering on, the harness pads the 1:1 render with its own black edge instead of cutting it, and the readback checks each short string.

params.prompt_or_change: "Unit 14B, Second Floor," "The Old Foundry Arts Centre," "127–129 St. John's Road," "Kingston upon Thames, KT1 2AB"

steps.why: The address is drawn by code character for character: the en dash, the period, the straight apostrophe and every comma. The four quoted lines become four lines (wrapped at 80% width), about 40 px on a 640x800 canvas. The overlay's 55% black box vanishes on the black ground, so the address reads as light text on black rather than a pasted band, and it sits in the empty lower half.

fix: (1) Harness, the lettering readback in execute.js and buildable.js: a garbled rendering of a WANTED string is a misspelling, never a 'stray' to remove. Fix one quoted line per edit, naming its position. Re-read after every fix, up to 2 rounds, and set the node 'flagged: lettering still wrong' instead of 'done / lettering fixed' when it still misreads. Drop fixText's hard-coded aspect_ratio 16:9 and its 'people, faces, poses, hands' wording for designs. (2) text-overlay: honour extra 'color: #hex; box: none; size: N' (the file header already promises 'box') so long exact text can be set in a design's own colours. (3) Planner rule and catalogue line: exact text over about 40 characters (an address, small print, terms) on a design is lettered by code. The image letters the short headline lines and leaves an empty zone, and text-overlay sets the long text, as a named exception to 'never a picture node plus a text-overlay'.
evidence: flyer_4x5.png (512x640, centre-cut from a 640x640 qwen render): headline, date and time are correct, with a curly ’ in Printmakers’. The address reads 'Unit 14B, Secomd' / 'Floor, [garbled] Arts Centre,' / '127–129 St. John’s Road' (no comma after Road) / 'Kingston  upon Thames, KT1 2AB'. The background is near-white rather than cream. flyer_source-before-text-fix.png is the first render: huge type filling the square, address lines 'Unit 14B, Second' and 'Floor, The Old Foundry Arts' correct, the remaining three lines garbled. exec.json shows the fix prompt asking qwen to letter the whole address and also to 'remove the Third address line … entirely … remove the Fourth address line … entirely … the people, faces, poses, hands … stay'. The fixed image shrank the block and broke lines 1–2. execute.js runs no readback after fixText. The judge was right overall (the address is garbled); faulting the curly apostrophe is over-strict typographically but did not change the verdict.
